analysis:
Examined the head text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 1-998) and the supplied patch excerpt. The visible change in the media path (head ~789-799, 821-824) computes reasoningPrefix from the rendered media prompt before bridge.submitTokenized, and passes a stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope) to the bridge. Previously this value was computed later (the base side reflects a move: ranges base 825-836 removed). The remaining changed ranges (head 1044-1046, 1428-1430) lie beyond the supplied excerpt, so they were not reviewed.

Security-relevant observations: the change only affects reasoning-parser state initialization and stop-string scoping. It does not change encryption, attestation, cache scope (requestCacheScope/cacheEnabled are still passed unchanged to submitTokenized, preserving T-041 scoping), the reservation release paths (mediaGate.release, releaseBox.fire on all error paths remain), or deadline checks. The tokenizer decode of the prompt tail is local and the result is not logged (promptPrepLogger metadata carries only sizes and timings, no content), consistent with A-001 handling. Reasoning prefix derivation uses only the local rendered prompt tokens; no new external input or attack surface is evident. No new plaintext exposure or authorization change.

Remaining questions for integration: the actual semantics of ReasoningStopScope.scope and the bridge's stopStringScope parameter, and the changed ranges at head 1044-1046 and 1428-1430 (outside the supplied text), could not be verified. A misconfigured stop scope would affect output correctness or truncation rather than confidentiality, so it is not a regression in a threat-model asset as far as can be seen. No findings.
